name: Japan
shortOverview: Japan is an island nation in East Asia known for its blend of cutting-edge technology, deep cultural traditions, and dramatic landscapes ranging from neon cities to quiet mountain villages.
funFacts: Japan is home to more than 6,800 islands, though most people live on just four of them.
High-speed Shinkansen trains have an average delay measured in seconds per year.
Vending machines are famously everywhere, offering everything from hot coffee to umbrellas.

name: France
shortOverview: France is a major European country known for its art, fashion, cuisine, and varied landscapes from Atlantic beaches to the Alps and Mediterranean coastline.
funFacts: France is the most visited country in the world by international tourists.
The Louvre in Paris is the largest art museum on Earth.
There are more types of French cheese than days in a year.

name: Brazil
shortOverview: Brazil is the largest country in South America, famous for the Amazon rainforest, vibrant cities like Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, and a strong football culture.
funFacts: Brazil shares borders with every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
The Amazon rainforest produces a significant share of the world's oxygen.
Rio's Christ the Redeemer statue is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

name: Kenya
shortOverview: Kenya is known for its wildlife-rich savannas, the Great Rift Valley, and highland regions that produce world-famous long-distance runners.
funFacts: The Great Migration of wildebeest passes through Kenya's Maasai Mara every year.
Mount Kenya is Africa's second-highest peak after Kilimanjaro.
Nairobi is one of the few world capitals with a national park on its doorstep.

name: Australia
shortOverview: Australia is a vast island continent known for its unique wildlife, laid-back coastal cities, and dramatic outback landscapes.
funFacts: Australia is roughly the same size as the continental United States but with a much smaller population.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on the planet.
More than 80% of Australians live within 100 km of the coast.
